paragraphs: Mentioned in Chullin 95b: he lost some tekhelet, blue-dyed wool, and afterwards found it. It had no identifying mark; he recognized it only by sight. He went to Rav Chisda to ask whether it was fit for use.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Visual recognition is distinguished from an identifying mark. The notice asks about fitness without giving the ruling.

Tekhelet means blue-dyed wool here. Hyman uses plural forms for the recovered pieces or threads; “recognition by sight” distinguishes familiarity with them from a specific identifying mark. The source supplies the question, without stating the ruling.
